requirements.note: Value rule conforms (empty or whitespace without leading "/" invalid, src/format/lsp-config.ts:69). But (1) the kit's validatePlugin (src/loading/validate/validate-plugin.ts) does not check inline lspServers entries at all: a probe of every row of §9.1.3 (unknown key, "gopls serve", "", {} map, "go" key, tcp, startupTimeout 0, requestTimeout 1.5, maxRestarts -1, env number) gave no finding; (2) the loader's message is the kit's ("must not contain spaces unless it starts with \"/\"; put arguments in \"args\""), not `Command should not contain spaces. Use args array for arguments.`; (3) an invalid inline map leaves the plugin loaded (see J9.5). Kit should change (spec text is the 2.1.325 oracle).

Value rules conform (at least one entry, keys start with ".", longest-match routing). The validator reports nothing for {} or a dotless key, and the loader message is the kit's ("needs at least one entry") instead of `extensionToLanguage must have at least one mapping`. Kit should change.
"stdio"|"socket" accepted, resolved transport always stdio (src/loading/resolve/lsp.ts:41).
Unset sends nothing (didChangeConfigurationOf), not substituted; when it is sent (once after initialized, again on reload) is the host LSP client's.
Substituted like command; unset stays unset in ResolvedLspServer and the host fills the project-root default (planLspStartup takes the host cwd). Compatible with the default the spec names.
Positive integer; unset stays unset (no deadline). Waiting and failing the start are the host LSP client's (kit judgment on lsp.ts).
Positive integer; unset means wait for the shutdown. Terminating is the host's.

The kit reports `Executable not found in $PATH: gopls` (src/loading/resolve/lsp-startup.ts:26); the spec and code-intelligence.md / troubleshooting.md quote the binary: `Executable not found in $PATH: "<binary>"`. The test only checks the prefix (tests/loading/resolve/lsp-startup.test.ts:63). The debug-log line `LSP server <name> failed to start: <reason>` is the host's. Kit should add the quotes.

A repeated name keeps the first entry at runtime (conforms to J9.7), but the kit's message is its own (`name "m" is already used by an earlier monitor; names must be unique within the plugin`), and its validatePlugin reports nothing for duplicate names in an inline array (probe), where the spec says the validator reports `Monitor names must be unique within a plugin` and fails. Kit should change.

Parsing conforms (exact "always" or "on-skill-invoke:<non-empty>", src/format/monitors.ts:43). Messages diverge: the kit reports `when: expected "always" or "on-skill-invoke:<skill>", got "<value>"` from the loader and nothing from validatePlugin (probe), where the spec (fixed in v05 from the 2.1.325 oracle) gives `on-skill-invoke: must specify a skill name` for an empty skill and also `Invalid string: must start with "on-skill-invoke:"` for any other value. Kit should change.

The refusal conforms exactly: template check before any value, the errors.md message verbatim (src/loading/resolve/shell-guard-monitor.ts:15), no option values exported, validator silent (J9.11). Divergence: with the default SubstitutionScope.shellPaths (`environment-reference`) the resolved monitor's `environment` carries the path variables its command references (src/loading/resolve/monitor.ts:30-36, 60), while §9.2.4 says the path variables are not exported to a monitor (manifest-reference "Not exported"). Low impact; either the kit substitutes in place by default, or the spec admits exporting exactly the referenced path variables as an equivalent technique.
